summary.text: 个 is the modern simplified form used chiefly as a general classifier for individual people and things. Traditional accounts connect it with bamboo-related 箇 and report 个 as an alternate form, but do not establish a complete graphic path to the modern character.

formation.text: Treat 个 as a whole graph in its current form. The traditional analysis of related 箇 is a different construction: 竹 marks the bamboo category and 固 supplies a sound cue. A transmitted commentary reports 个 as an alternate form meaning half a bamboo; this does not prove a whole-graph borrowing from a bamboo object-name.

components.text: The current graph is treated as a whole, not divided into a tally and a person. Such a decomposition is proposed in one modern note, but is not supported as the graph’s historical construction here.
In related 箇, 竹 marks the bamboo category in the transmitted analysis. The curated seal-script-style form illustrates 箇 with 竹 above 固; it is a modern redraw, not a dated stage in 个’s development.

In 箇, 固 is identified as the sound element. Its reconstructed form is similar to, but not identical with, that of 箇; this supports phonetic compatibility, not the original name of a bamboo object or a proven whole-graph loan.

sound_limitation.text: The comparison supports sound compatibility in this reconstruction system, but does not establish a bamboo object’s original spoken name or prove borrowing of the whole graph from that name.

sound.text: The Baxter–Sagart forms are related but not identical; modern Mandarin also differs in tone.

history.text: The curated image shows a modern redraw of 箇 in a transmitted Shuowen seal-script style, with 竹 above 固. It illustrates that traditional analysis, not a securely dated stage in 个’s graphic history.

The transmitted lexicographic account reports 个 as an alternate form for half a bamboo, while a variant dictionary catalogs 个 as a variant of 個. These accounts do not establish a complete graphic sequence connecting 箇, 個 and modern 个.

uncertainties.text: No character-specific oracle-bone or bronze form or dated graphic path from the bamboo-related account to modern 个 is established here; this does not show that earlier forms never existed.

A bamboo-related counting use and a separate ritual counting use are recorded, but neither their chronology nor a continuous development into the general classifier is established. A research abstract proposes a more complex history.
No independently recoverable spoken name for the proposed bamboo object is established. Similar recorded or reconstructed readings make a sound-based borrowing possible, but do not demonstrate it.

senses.text: A transmitted commentary reports this meaning for 个 in an alternate-form account. It is not independently established as the character’s earliest meaning.
A cited classical passage is associated by commentary with counting bamboo. It does not establish the first attestation or a transition to the general classifier.

senses.gloss: counting item or unit, like 枚
senses.text: A ritual counting context is reported with 个 glossed as comparable to 枚. The available evidence does not date this sense or connect it to bamboo-related counting.

senses.gloss: general classifier for individual people or things
senses.text: 个 is used as a general classifier for counting people and objects. Its emergence is not dated here.
A current sense meaning ‘single’ or ‘individual’ is recorded. Its historical relation to the classifier is not established here.

limitations.text: The recorded historical counting uses cannot be placed in a secure sequence, and no semantic bridge from bamboo-related counting to general classifier use is established; no development is asserted.
Modern dictionaries also record demonstrative and particle uses, but no dated sequence connects them to the older counting uses.
